disease_label_per_paper: Bartonella quintana culture-negative endocarditis with multivalve disease, embolic strokes, suspected mycotic aneurysm, and valve replacement
presentation_summary: 37-year-old African man originally from the Democratic Republic of Congo was transferred with aortic valve vegetation, multiple embolic strokes, and possible brain mycotic aneurysm.
He had two weeks of progressive shortness of breath and chest pain, occasional night sweats, fatigue, 10-lb weight loss over six months, and intermittent sharp chest pain radiating to the neck.
Exam showed cachexia, 4/6 systolic murmur radiating to the axilla, palpable thrill, 3/6 diastolic murmur, Janeway lesions on both feet/soles, and L4-L5 lumbar tenderness.
Initial labs included WBC 5 x10^9/L, hemoglobin 8.9 g/dL, hematocrit 27%, and three negative blood-culture sets; RF was 83 U/mL.

TEE showed a mobile aortic valve vegetation with severe aortic and mitral regurgitation plus mitral stenosis/thickening; CT showed bilateral pleural effusions, cardiomegaly, hepatosplenomegaly, periportal lymphadenopathy, and splenic wedge-shaped lesions; brain MRI showed acute/subacute infarcts and suspected mycotic aneurysm.
Bartonella serology was strongly positive and B. quintana was confirmed by mitral valve PCR and extended culture after 21 days; he underwent aortic and mitral valve replacements.

quality_warnings: Bartonella serology, valve PCR, and extended culture are confirmatory_findings, not ordinary observations.
The case preserves embolic stroke, suspected mycotic aneurysm, splenic infarct, severe multivalve regurgitation, and surgery need as ordinary pathophysiology evidence.
